images.title: The bump rule: 1 side becomes 4
images.purpose: Shows the Koch bump rule on a single side: a side of length 1 is cut into thirds and the middle third is replaced by two sides of a small equilateral triangle, giving 4 sides of length 1/3.
images.composition: Plain white background with generous empty margins; the main object is large and centred and fills about 60 percent of the frame; nothing else is drawn. Before and after in one row: a straight segment on the left, a thick grey arrow, the bumped segment on the right, both the same overall width.
images.exact_structure: Left: one thick straight horizontal teal #0072B2 segment, 6 units long, with 2 small grey tick marks dividing it into 3 equal parts of 2 units. Above its middle: '1'. Below it: '1 side'. Centre: a thick grey arrow pointing right. Right: a thick amber #E69F00 path of the same overall width made of exactly 4 straight segments, each 2 units long: a flat segment, then a segment rising at 60°, then a segment falling at 60° (these two form the upper sides of an equilateral triangle sitting on the empty middle third), then a flat segment. The empty middle third is shown as a faint dashed grey line (the removed part). Each of the 4 amber segments has '1/3' next to it in small dark text: 4 times. Below the path: '4 sides'. Nothing else.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Every side becomes 4 sides, each one third as long.
images.description: Shows the Koch bump rule on a single side: a side of length 1 is cut into thirds and the middle third is replaced by two sides of a small equilateral triangle, giving 4 sides of length 1/3.
images.context: Concept T4.C1; one image that shows only the main idea.
images.teaching_notes: Step 1 from a triangle of side 1: 3 × 4 = 12 sides, perimeter 12 × 1/3 = 4 units.

image_decisions.why: The bump rule is a geometric replacement; one side before and after shows exactly what changes.
